drafted_by: AI, requires clinician review before any real use.

questions.text: What is the main problem: fever, night sweats, weight loss, severe fatigue, or feeling generally unwell?
questions.rationale: Clarifying the main constitutional complaint guides the next branch of the interview.

questions.text: When did this start, and has it been getting better, worse, or staying the same?
questions.rationale: Duration separates self-limited infection from prolonged fever or occult disease.

questions.text: Have you measured a fever, how high, and does it come and go or stay through the day?
questions.rationale: Documented fever pattern helps triage infection versus other causes.

questions.text: Do you soak the sheets with sweats at night?
questions.rationale: Drenching night sweats raise concern for TB, lymphoma, or endocarditis.

questions.text: Have you lost weight without trying? How much, over how long?
questions.rationale: Unintended weight loss needs a systematic workup.

questions.text: Is the fatigue new, and does it prevent usual activities even after rest?
questions.rationale: Disabling fatigue with other B symptoms is more concerning than tiredness alone.

questions.text: Has your appetite dropped, or do clothes fit looser?
questions.rationale: Anorexia with weight loss supports systemic illness.

questions.text: Any cough, burning urine, diarrhea, rash, stiff neck, or localized pain with the fever?
questions.rationale: Localizing symptoms point to a source of infection.

questions.text: Have you had shaking chills, or do you feel very ill right now?
questions.rationale: Rigors and toxic appearance raise concern for bacteremia.

questions.text: Have you traveled, been around sick people, ticks, animals, or untreated water?
questions.rationale: Travel and exposure history expands the infectious differential.

questions.text: Have you been around someone with TB, been in jail or a shelter, or had a positive TB test?
questions.rationale: TB risk matters for prolonged fever and night sweats.

questions.text: Do you have HIV, cancer, or take steroids or other immune-suppressing medicine?
questions.rationale: Immunosuppression broadens infection and cancer risk.

questions.text: Have you noticed swollen glands, a lump, or abdominal fullness?
questions.rationale: Lymphadenopathy or mass with B symptoms raises concern for lymphoma.

questions.text: Any unusual bruising, bleeding, or pallor?
questions.rationale: These suggest a blood disorder accompanying constitutional symptoms.

questions.text: Do you have a heart valve problem, or have you used injection drugs?
questions.rationale: These raise pretest probability of endocarditis.

questions.text: Any new rash, joint pain or swelling, or mouth ulcers?
questions.rationale: These point toward autoimmune or reactive disease.

questions.text: Have you had cancer, or a strong family history of cancer?
questions.rationale: Cancer history changes the meaning of fever and weight loss.

questions.text: Have you started any new medicines, including antibiotics or over-the-counter drugs?
questions.rationale: Drug fever and side effects are common in prolonged illness.

questions.text: How are your mood and sleep, and is the fatigue more like low mood than physical illness?
questions.rationale: Depression can present as fatigue and weight change and should be asked explicitly.

questions.text: Are you much thirstier, more sensitive to heat or cold, or have you noticed neck swelling?
questions.rationale: Thyroid and diabetes can present as constitutional symptoms.

questions.text: How much alcohol or other drugs do you use?
questions.rationale: Alcohol and drugs cause fever, weight loss, and fatigue.

questions.text: If this is fever, has it lasted more than three weeks without a clear cause?
questions.rationale: Prolonged unexplained fever needs a broader workup than a short viral illness.

questions.text: Are you able to eat, drink, and get out of bed, or are you getting weaker quickly?
questions.rationale: Rapid functional decline raises urgency.

questions.text: What is the main thing you are worried this could be?
questions.rationale: Understanding the patient's concern guides reassurance and follow-up questions.

red_flags.label: Fever with shaking chills or looking very ill
red_flags.detection_instructions: Does the patient report high fever with shaking chills or feeling extremely ill?

red_flags.label: Unintended weight loss
red_flags.detection_instructions: Does the patient report losing a substantial amount of weight without trying?

red_flags.label: Night sweats with lumps or prolonged fever
red_flags.detection_instructions: Does the patient report drenching night sweats with swollen glands or fever lasting weeks?

red_flags.label: Fever with valve disease or injection drug use
red_flags.detection_instructions: Does the patient report fever with a known heart valve problem or injection drug use?

red_flags.label: Fever with a weakened immune system
red_flags.detection_instructions: Does the patient report fever while having HIV, cancer, or taking immune-suppressing medicine?

red_flags.label: Rapid decline in ability to function
red_flags.detection_instructions: Does the patient say they cannot eat, drink, or get out of bed, or are weakening quickly?
